title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook codifies Redwood's end-to-end applied ML evaluation workflow: onboarding models into the eval-harness, authoring and maintaining prompt sets and benchmarks, producing quantization profiles, and running regression triage when quality drops are detected. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML reviewers, and SREs who support model serving.

Scope
- Eval harness integration and quality gates
- Prompt set creation and benchmark maintenance
- Quantization profile generation and validation
- Regression detection, triage, and rollback/runbook steps

Key goals
- Reduce time to onboard a model to production-safe quality (target: < 3 business days for baseline models)
- Detect regressions within 24 hours of rollout at 95% confidence
- Provide reproducible, auditable evals and remediation steps

Owner and stakeholders
- Playbook owner: Applied ML Infrastructure (applied-ml team)
- Primary stakeholders: Model owners, Serving Runtime, Observability, Product QA
- Escalation: oncall-applied-ml -> eng-platform -> eng-sre (see Oncall and Incident Response docs)

Glossary
- Eval harness: Redwood's internal evaluation suite (service: eval-harness) that runs prompt sets, metrics, and guardrails against model artifacts.
- Prompt set: A curated set of instructions + canonical expected outputs used to measure model quality for a specific capability.
- Quantization profile: A set of tuning parameters and representative token sequences used to validate 8-bit/4-bit quantized model performance and quality.
- Regression triage: The cross-functional process for investigating and remediating observed quality degradations after a model change.

1) Onboarding a new model to the Eval Harness

Summary
Follow these steps when bringing a model artifact (e.g., v1.3.0-llama2-13b-q4f) into the eval-harness for evaluation and readiness checks prior to a canary rollout. Estimated time: 2-8 hours for initial pass.

Preconditions
- Model artifact uploaded to model registry (service: model-registry) with checksum and schema metadata.
- CI build for model container image passes unit tests and security scan.

Steps
1. Create eval-harness job spec
   - Template: eval-job-template.yaml (see example below)
   - Fields: model_name, model_version, quantization_profile, benchmark_list, resources (gpus/cpu), timeout
2. Run baseline evaluation with canonical prompt sets
   - CLI: eval-harness run --job ./eval-job.yaml --env staging
   - Metrics collected: accuracy, exact_match, rouge-L, perplexity, harmful_score, latency_p50/p95/p99
3. Validate quality guardrails (see section 3)
4. Generate quantization profile candidate (if quantized)
   - Use representative tokens: sample from production prefix cache or synthetic generation (see Quantization Profiling below)
5. Register eval report to artifacts storage and attach to model-registry entry

Example eval-job-template.yaml (shortened)
```yaml
model_name: "llama2-13b"
model_version: "v1.3.0-llama2-13b-q4f"
benchmarks: ["summarization-core-2028", "safety-checklist-2028"]
quantization_profile: "q4f-profile-2028-10"
resources:
  gpus: 1
  mem_gb: 64
timeout: 7200
```

Acceptance criteria (pass to proceed to canary)
- No safety-critical violations (harmful_score < 0.01 on safety-checklist)
- Core benchmarks: accuracy and rouge-L must be within -2% of baseline (reference model)
- Latency p95 within 1.3x of reference latency on Dedicated profile

Owner: Applied ML + Model Owner

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarks: creation and maintenance

Best practices for prompt sets
- Aim for 200-2,000 examples per capability (smaller capability sets acceptable with stronger unit tests)
- Include positive/negative cases, edge cases, and adversarial probes
- Label examples with expected output and scoring rubric (exact match, normalized-bleu, or semantic-similarity)
- Store prompt sets in Git repo: git@repo:redwood/applied-ml/prompt-sets

Prompt set metadata table (example)
| field | description | example |
|------|-------------|---------|
| id | short name | summarization-core-2028 |
| capability | high-level capability | summarization |
| owner | owning team | applied-ml |
| examples | # of examples | 1200 |
| evaluation_metric | primary metric | rouge-L |
| created_at | date | 2028-04-10 |

Maintenance cadence
- Quarterly review for high-traffic capabilities
- Immediate review on detection of systematic failure (see regression triage)
- PR reviewers: capability owner + applied-ml-reviewer

3) Quality Guardrails and Thresholds

Guardrail categories
- Safety: toxic/hate, instruction abuse, PII leakage
- Correctness: factuality, hallucination rate, task-specific accuracy
- Stability: latency, tokenization regressions, memory errors

SLOs and hard thresholds
- Safety violations: safety-violation-rate <= 0.01 on safety-checklist benchmark (hard fail)
- Task accuracy delta: no more than -2.0% relative to baseline for core benchmarks (soft fail requires signoff)
- Latency p95: <= 1.5x baseline (soft fail below this threshold requires optimization)
- Memory OOMs: 0 per 10k requests (hard fail)

Automated enforcement
- Eval-harness posts results to eval-results topic (Kafka) and to model-registry metadata.
- CI gating: if any hard fail metrics are present, the model cannot be promoted to canary branch.
- Alerting: Regression alert triggers if a metric delta exceeds soft-fail thresholds and persists across two consecutive runs.

4) Quantization Profiles and Validation

Purpose
Provide repeatable quantization config and representative inputs so that quantized models meet accuracy and latency expectations.

Profile contents
- algorithm: awq | q4f | q8_hybrid
- representative_sequences: list of tokenized prefixes (see example)
- per-layer calibration flags
- validation_benchmarks: list of benchmark ids to run after quantization

Representative sequence sampling
1. Sample 10k prefixes from production KV cache (anonymized) avoiding PII and customer identifiers.
2. Augment with synthetic sequences for low-frequency capabilities.
3. Store tokenized sequences in profile artifact attached to model-registry.

Validation checklist
- Run quantized model on validation_benchmarks and compare against float baseline.
- Quality delta thresholds: task accuracy delta <= 1.5% and safety delta <= 0.005 absolute.
- Latency improvement target: p95 decrease >= 1.1x for cost justification.

Example quantization-profile (yaml snippet)
```yaml
profile_id: q4f-profile-2028-10
algorithm: q4f
representative_sequences: "s3://eval-artifacts/rep-seqs/q4f-profile-2028-10/rep.txt"
per_layer_rounding: true
validation_benchmarks: ["summarization-core-2028", "safety-checklist-2028"]
```

Owner: Applied ML + Runtime Kernel Team

5) Regression Triage Playbook (detection -> remediation -> rollout)

Triggers
- Canary metrics cross soft-fail thresholds for two consecutive eval runs
- Post-deploy monitoring (console/observability) shows production metric delta > threshold for 1 hour
- Customer-reported regression with validated reproducible prompt

Initial triage (first 30-60 minutes)
1. Triage owner assigned: oncall-applied-ml.
2. Retrieve failing examples and eval reports from eval-results topic and model-registry.
3. Run narrow reproduction locally with same model artifact and prompt set: eval-harness reproduce --model <id> --prompt-ids <list>
4. Classify failure into bucket: safety / correctness / latency / memory / tokenization.

Triage matrix and ownership
| Category | First responder | SLA | Example action |
| Safety | Applied-ML + Security | 1 hour | Revert canary, block promotion, open security incident |
| Correctness | Model Owner + Applied-ML | 4 hours | Re-run with smaller beam/temp, compare to baseline, inspect quantization profile |
| Latency | Runtime + SRE | 4 hours | Adjust batch size, examine kernel selection, revert to CPU fallback if needed |
| Memory | Runtime + Infra | 2 hours | Reduce max_seq_length, check for KV cache growth, rollback |

Remediation steps (ordered)
1. If safety critical: immediate revert to previous model and open security incident.
2. If correctness from quantization: re-run quantization with stricter calibration or use higher-precision fallback.
3. If performance: adjust autoscaling/batching settings and monitor for improvement.
4. If unknown: create a reproducible test case, raise to Model Review Board (MRB) with full eval artifacts.

Communication and runbook updates
- Update incident ticket with eval report links, failing prompt ids, and remediation attempt logs.
- If a rollback occurs, update model-registry with note and tag previous model as active.
- Post-mortem required for regressions that impact > 1% of production traffic or last > 12 hours.

6) Metrics, dashboards, and alerting

Key metrics to display on Applied ML dashboards
- Benchmark pass rate by model and by capability
- Safety violation rate (daily and rolling 7d)
- Accuracy delta vs. baseline (rolling 24h)
- Quantization validation success rate
- Canary vs. baseline latency p95/p99

Example alert rules (Prometheus-style pseudocode)
- Alert: EvalSafetyViolation
  expr: safety_violation_rate{env="prod"} > 0.01 for 5m
  severity: critical
- Alert: ModelAccuracyRegression
  expr: (baseline_accuracy - model_accuracy) > 0.02 for 10m
  severity: high

7) Auditing and compliance

- All eval runs produce an immutable eval-report JSON stored in S3: s3://eval-reports/{model}/{run_id}.json
- Model-registry must include links to eval reports and quantization artifacts before promotion.
- For customer-sensitive models (confidentiality: restricted), require KMS-wrapped artifacts and access control lists.

8) Playbook governance and cadence

- Quarterly review by Applied ML Infrastructure and Applied ML Review Board.
- All changes to thresholds or guardrails require a documented ADR and reviewer approvals (min 2 reviewers).
- Training: bi-annual training sessions for oncall-applied-ml and new model owners.

Appendix A: Useful CLI snippets
- Run a full benchmark locally:
  eval-harness run --model llama2-13b --benchmarks summarization-core-2028,safety-checklist-2028 --out ./reports/llama2-13b-baseline.json
- Reproduce a failing prompt:
  eval-harness reproduce --model <model-id> --prompt-id <prompt-id> --seed 42 --out ./repro.json
- Generate quantization candidate:
  quantize-tool --model ./float-model.pt --profile q4f-profile-2028-10 --out ./model-q4f.pt

Appendix B: Contacts and escalation list
- Applied ML oncall: #oncall-applied-ml (PagerDuty)
- Runtime oncall: #oncall-runtime (PagerDuty)
- Security: security-response@redwood.com

Appendix C: Example failure case and postmortem checklist
1. Summary of incident
2. Timeline (detection -> triage -> remediation -> rollback -> postmortem)
3. Root cause analysis (quantization algorithm, model change, data drift, infra)
4. Action items and owners
5. Regression tests to add to prompt sets

References
- eval-harness standards: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Quantization best practices: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026
- Model registry runbook: /confluence/eng-infra/model-registry-runbook

End of document
